findings.title: Fallback locales are loaded only during web requests
findings.body: I18n.translate loads only config.locale before delegating to the backend, while the new code loads the site-default and English fallback files only from ApplicationController#set_locale. Background jobs, mailers, rake tasks, console code, and model-level translations therefore query fallback locales whose YAML files were never loaded and receive 'translation missing'. Worse, argument-less lookups cache that missing result in the LRU cache at lines 71-76, so the missing string can persist after a later web request loads the fallback locale. Fallback loading belongs in the translation/load path, not only in the controller.

findings.title: Every fallback lookup depends on SiteSetting and can fail outside a ready request stack
findings.body: FallbackLocaleList#[] unconditionally calls SiteSetting.default_locale.to_sym, and I18n::Backend::Fallbacks invokes this method for translation misses in any context, not just after ApplicationController has already resolved the locale. If the setting is blank or the settings/DB layer is unavailable during boot, migrations, seeding, or job startup, a routine missing translation becomes a NoMethodError or database error instead of falling back to :en. The hot missing-translation path should use a guarded or cached default that safely degrades to English.

findings.title: Cached translations ignore the dynamic fallback chain
findings.body: The LRU cache key contains only the key, current locale, and backend object_id, but after this change the result for a key missing in the current locale also depends on SiteSetting.default_locale, which FallbackLocaleList reads dynamically. Changing the site default locale does not change the cache key or clear the cache, so users can keep receiving text in the previous fallback language until entries are evicted or translations are manually reloaded.

findings.title: No tests cover the new fallback behaviour
findings.body: The pull request introduces a custom FallbackLocaleList, backend Fallbacks inclusion, fallback-file loading, and a controller hook, but adds no specs. There is no coverage proving that a key missing in the user locale resolves first to the site default and then to English, that fallback locale files are loaded before lookup, or that pluralized/interpolated fallback translations work, so regressions would silently surface as 'translation missing' text.
